key_points.point: The document highlights the goal of developing artificial intelligence systems that surpass human capabilities across broad domains, moving rapidly toward artificial general intelligence within this decade. This capability surge is driven by frontier labs aiming to automate their own research and development pipelines to achieve exponential recursive self-improvement. Accelerationists view this as the primary engine for technological abundance and economic supremacy, where automating AI researchers themselves creates decisive competitive advantages. However, the text notes that this rapid internal scaling occurs entirely behind closed doors without external transparency or robust governance.
key_points.verbatim: According to these companies and independent experts, future AI systems may become so capable that they could reach or even surpass human intelligence and capabilities by 2030... OpenAI CEO Sam Altman writes that "in 2025, we may see the first AI agents 'join the workforce' and materially change the output of companies".
key_points.canonical_proposition: It is necessary to build advanced AI systems that surpass human versatility and automate core research and development pipelines.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within accelerationist discourse that prioritizes the engineering of artificial intelligence systems possessing cross-domain generalization and fluid adaptability exceeding human baselines to automate core research and development pipelines. Encompasses: Automated research pipelines, recursive self-improvement.

key_points.point: Frontier AI companies are experiencing a winner-takes-all economic dynamic driven by the ability of advanced AI systems to write software and accelerate engineering velocity internally. The document asserts that companies furthest ahead in capability scaling are best positioned to leverage internal deployment to pull even further ahead of competitors. This creates strong commercial incentives for labs to taper down external public releases in favor of exclusive internal application. Accelerationists rely on this self-reinforcing feedback loop of proprietary automation as the primary vehicle for rapid technological takeoff.
key_points.verbatim: As a byproduct of this trend, the internal deployment of highly advanced AI systems will likely yield a number of economic advantages, such as a "winner takes all" dynamic enabled by automated AI research and development... and give rise to the pursuit of strategic incentives, including competitive non-transparency.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Internal deployment of frontier AI creates an insurmountable winner-takes-all competitive advantage through recursive self-improvement and automated R&D.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that internal deployment of advanced artificial intelligence generates an insurmountable winner-takes-all competitive advantage through automated research and development. Encompasses: Winner-takes-all dynamics, automated software generation.

key_points.point: The document asserts that internal deployment of advanced AI systems allows developers to bypass public-facing safety restrictions and consumer-focused guardrails in order to maximize productivity and accelerate technological progress toward artificial general intelligence. By focusing exclusively on internal operations, AI companies can leverage high-powered models—such as helpful-only or under-assessed base models—without being slowed down by traditional external compliance requirements. This strategic approach aligns directly with accelerationist goals of rapid capability scaling and the automation of vital research labor, treating safety constraints as secondary to the overarching race for competitive dominance and technological supremacy.
key_points.verbatim: In principle, AI systems can be deployed at any stage of safety development, including prior to the application of these safeguards. Therefore, any of these safeguards could, in theory, be absent in internally deployed highly advanced AI systems. This means that, on top of being comparatively æunder-assessedÆ for the threats they may pose, highly advanced AI systems that enable internal applications could be covered by a different set of safeguards than those externally deployed.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve rapid capability scaling by prioritizing internal AI deployment without public safety constraints.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that prioritizes internal AI deployment to maximize technological progress and capability scaling without external safety constraints. Encompasses: Bypassing public-facing guardrails, automating critical research labor, and accelerating the pursuit of artificial general intelligence.

key_points.point: The report highlights that the primary economic driver for internal deployment is the automation of scarce and costly labor, specifically AI researchers and software engineers, which will dramatically accelerate innovation velocity. Industry leaders such as John Schulman and Mark Zuckerberg project that AI systems will soon perform the vast majority of coding and technical research, effectively substituting for millions of human workers. From an accelerationist perspective, this labor substitution creates an unprecedented multiplier effect on productivity, transforming AI companies into hyper-scaled operations capable of achieving AGI at a fraction of traditional timelines.
key_points.verbatim: First, at a given future point in AI development, there will likely be outsized economic benefits to the exclusive internal deployment of highly advanced AI systems. One of those outsized benefits may be the automation of the scarcest and highest-value labor to a frontier AI company: AI researchers themselves.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Internal deployment of frontier AI automates scarce research labor and exponentially accelerates technological progress toward artificial general intelligence.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that internal AI deployment drives exponential productivity gains by automating high-value cognitive labor. Encompasses: Substituting human researchers, accelerating R&D velocity, and achieving decisive competitive advantages in AI development.

key_points.point: The document details how internally deployed AI systems can act through virtual and physical actuators, writing code, executing experiments, and managing repositories autonomously. Accelerationists view this autonomous integration as essential for scaling agentic productivity from pilot phases into core operational workflows. By granting advanced AI systems broad access to compute, software tools, and web resources, organizations achieve transformative acceleration in output and engineering velocity. However, this high degree of agency increases systemic risk profiles and challenges traditional oversight frameworks.
key_points.verbatim: Execute permission: using virtual and physical affordances. Internally deployed AI systems may also be enabled to autonomously commit and push the code they have written to the internal repository to encourage a frictionless process.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve rapid productivity scaling by deploying autonomous AI agents with virtual and physical execution permissions across enterprise workflows.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that champions the deployment of autonomous AI agents with execution permissions to drive enterprise velocity and operational autonomy. Encompasses: Autonomous code commit, virtual actuators, and frictionless workflow integration.

key_points.point: The text explains how automated AI research and development creates a self-reinforcing loop where models iteratively design, train, and improve their successors. Accelerationists strongly endorse this transition, arguing that substituting human bottlenecks with automated machine learning and neural architecture search is vital for technological progress. As AI systems take over the AI R&D pipeline, research velocity increases exponentially, bypassing traditional human limitations. Nonetheless, this rapid scaling compounds the difficulty of auditing complex technological outputs.
key_points.verbatim: Once AI systems become a significant contributor to the AI R&D process, this could enable a self-reinforcing loop where increasingly capable AI systems play a growing role in designing their successors.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve exponential technological progress by scaling automated AI research and development pipelines to design successive model generations.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that prioritizes the automation of artificial intelligence research and development to establish self-reinforcing capability scaling loops. Encompasses: Automated machine learning, neural architecture search, and recursive model self-improvement.

key_points.point: The text examines how highly advanced AI systems can be applied to partially or fully automate the AI R&D process, functioning as an amplifier for runaway progress and creating a self-reinforcing feedback loop. By utilizing automated researchers to accomplish tasks faster than humans, AI companies can iteratively produce more capable systems at an accelerating rate. This capability scaling is framed as a driver of rapid technological advancement, though the document notes it presents significant oversight and preparedness challenges. Accelerationists view this compounding feedback loop as a mechanism for achieving rapid capability gains, even if the text highlights the resulting governance pressures.
key_points.verbatim: In this Section, we examine two likely consequences of a scenario where a highly advanced AI system is used to partially or fully automate AI R&D. The application of such an AI system to automate the AI R&D process pipeline presents as an amplifier to both threats: (i) runaway AI progress; and (ii) uncontrolled power accumulation by an AI system itself.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve rapid capability gains by means of automating the AI research and development pipeline with advanced AI systems.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that utilizes advanced artificial intelligence systems to automate the research and development pipeline, generating a self-reinforcing feedback loop of recursive self-improvement and rapid capability gains. Encompasses: algorithmic efficiency scaling, automated research agents, recursive self-improvement loops.

key_points.point: The document models the exponential growth of algorithmic efficiency using historical data and projections, assuming a baseline 3x improvement each year that could be accelerated to 9x annually through automated AI R&D. This quantitative modeling relies on smoothing assumptions about exponential progress over time to project future capability milestones. While the text uses this back-of-the-envelope calculation to illustrate extreme velocity, accelerationists interpret such compounding returns as evidence of inevitable technological takeoff.
key_points.verbatim: For the BOTEC, we assume that the highly advanced AI system triples the rate of progress on algorithmic efficiency and does so continuously over time. If we use an estimate of current algorithmic progress as an exponential 3x improvement each year (Ho et al. 2024), then the use of the AI system for AI R&D means that the rate of algorithmic progress increases to 9x a year, likely accompanied by significant capability improvements.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Automated AI R&D compounds algorithmic efficiency improvements exponentially, transforming linear progress into rapid capability takeoffs.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that recursive automation of research and development compounds algorithmic efficiency improvements exponentially, driving rapid capability takeoffs. Encompasses: exponential algorithmic scaling, quantitative feedback modeling, recursive acceleration.

key_points.point: The text highlights the unprecedented capabilities of internal workforces enabled by advanced AI, such as a 'country of geniuses in a data center' operating at high velocities. This reflects the accelerationist belief that AI integration will drive massive economic expansion and productivity through scalable cognitive labor. These systems can be replicated, operate continuously, and outperform human enterprises. However, the report frames this concentration of productive capacity as a severe governance and national security challenge. Accelerationists view this expansive capability as the core engine of future prosperity, even if the report warns of unprecedented disruption.
key_points.verbatim: Indeed, the potential development of a 'country of geniuses in a data center' (Amodei 2024)—highly capable company-internal workforces applied predominantly to advancing organizational goals—raises some concerns about the magnitude and high velocity of economic concentration and disruption this could yield.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI integration into internal corporate workforces drives massive economic expansion and productive capacity through continuous, scalable cognitive labor.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that the integration of artificial intelligence into internal corporate workforces drives massive economic expansion and productive capacity through continuous, scalable cognitive labor. Encompasses: company-internal workforces, scalable cognitive labor, economic expansion.

key_points.point: AI companies are actively transitioning to primarily AI-powered internal workforces to accelerate organizational goals and operational capabilities. This strategy leverages software optimizations and intelligence explosions behind closed doors to achieve rapid progress without relying on external hardware buildouts. Accelerationists champion this approach to maximize efficiency and outcompete traditional human-based enterprises. Nevertheless, the document notes that this internal velocity bypasses traditional monitoring and creates severe regulatory challenges.
key_points.verbatim: As AI companies transition to primarily AI-powered internal workforces, they could create concentrations of productive capacity unprecedented in economic history. Unlike human workers who face physical, cognitive, and temporal limitations, AI systems can be replicated at scale, operate continuously, and potentially perform intellectual tasks at speeds and volumes impossible for human workers.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Accelerate organizational goals and operational capabilities by transitioning to AI-powered internal workforces that operate continuously at unprecedented speeds.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that champions the transition to AI-powered internal workforces to accelerate organizational goals and operational capabilities continuously. Encompasses: AI-powered internal workforces, continuous operation, accelerated capability development.

key_points.point: The document examines how existing regulatory frameworks like the EU AI Act and TRAIGA can be construed to cover internal deployment by interpreting 'putting into service' or 'putting into effect' as making AI available exclusively for the developing organization. While the authors note they do not advocate for an extensive interpretation at present, this legal mapping illustrates a strategy of extending established regulatory concepts to new technological domains. For accelerationists, this highlights the tension between applying legacy statutory definitions to rapidly evolving AI capabilities versus letting innovation proceed without pre-market friction. However, analogizing AI governance to traditional industrial sectors may impose compliance burdens that slow down developmental velocity.
key_points.verbatim: In summary, the AI Act and the TRAIGA could apply not only to AI systems and AI models that are publicly released and commercialized (”plac[ing] in the market”) but also to AI systems that are ”put into service” or ”into effect” for the developer’s ”own use.”
key_points.canonical_proposition: Apply existing statutory definitions of commercial release and deployment to cover internal AI R&D activities.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that examines how existing regulatory frameworks can be interpreted to encompass internal deployment. Encompasses: Statutory definitions of putting into service, adapting market release rules for internal use.

key_points.point: The document asserts that safety interventions for frontier AI should rely on flexible, company-led tripwires rather than heavy-handed government mandates, allowing innovation to proceed unhindered until specific risk thresholds are met. By structuring internal governance around empirical tripwires, companies can maintain development velocity while applying targeted mitigations only when dangerous capabilities like scheming materialize. This approach aligns with accelerationist goals of preserving commercial momentum and avoiding preemptive bureaucratic sclerosis while still addressing catastrophic tail risks. However, the report cautions that as capabilities scale toward AGI and potential power accumulation risks increase, lighter-touch company frameworks may eventually need supplementation by government oversight.
verbatim: All these solutions are company-led and constructed around "tripwires," which means that no action is required from companies unless certain trigger conditions are met (Karnofsky 2024).
This makes our current proposal flexible and non-invasive.
Companies can keep innovating and adopt mitigations only when pathways to specific threat-relevant scenarios start to manifest (Pistillo and Stix 2024).
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI governance ought to rely on flexible, company-led tripwires and conditional mitigations that preserve innovation velocity while addressing empirically demonstrated risk thresholds.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within accelerationist discourse that prioritizes flexible, company-led governance structures utilizing empirical tripwires and conditional mitigations to preserve innovation velocity while addressing demonstrable risk thresholds. Encompasses: Flexible regulatory frameworks, company-led compliance tripwires, innovation-preserving governance structures.

key_points.point: The document outlines governance frameworks and mechanisms for internal AI deployment that can be tied into broader public-private partnerships and licensing arrangements. By establishing structured oversight, evaluation-triggered tripwires, and security baselines, AI companies can build mutually beneficial relationships with government entities. This collaboration can unlock strategic resources such as secure energy, specialized land use, expedited permitting, and specialized databases. These mechanisms support rapid capability scaling and secure development while aligning private innovation with national security priorities.
key_points.verbatim: In short, we propose that well-thought-through and executed governance of internal deployment can, under certain conditions, create a situation of mutual benefit for AI companies and governments alike. In particular, we see this fit into, for example, traditional frameworks of public-private partnership or, more nascent, proposals around AI licensing regimes (Bipartisan Framework on AI Legislation 2023).
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve robust AI capability scaling and resource access by means of structured public-private partnerships and governance frameworks.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that secures strategic governmental resources and public-private collaboration through structured internal deployment governance and compliance frameworks. Encompasses: public-private partnerships, licensing regimes, and resource access.

key_points.point: The document proposes that transparency regarding who accesses internal AI systems can be achieved by sharing internal usage policies with select internal staff and government agencies. This targeted visibility allows verification of access restrictions and supports early warning mechanisms to prevent downstream harm. By establishing clear access boundaries and usage guidelines, companies can maintain operational efficiency while satisfying regulatory oversight requirements. However, overly restrictive internal sharing policies could potentially slow down internal R&D cycles if compliance burdens become too heavy.
key_points.verbatim: Previously (º6.2.(b)), we explained how internal usage policies could establish guidelines that dictate how, when, and by whom internally deployed AI systems may be accessed and utilized within an AI company. Hence, from examining internal usage policies, a reader (i.e., staff allowed to access and use internal AI systems and potentially a select government agency) could understand who within an AI company can access its most capable AI systems.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve transparent internal AI governance by means of sharing internal usage policies with designated staff and government agencies.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advocates for disclosure-based internal usage policies paired with selective stakeholder access to create verifiable operational boundaries. Encompasses: Internal usage guidelines, selective stakeholder visibility, access control verification.

key_points.point: The text discusses pre-deployment safety cases as structured, evidence-based rationales demonstrating that an AI system deployed to a specific setting is unlikely to cause catastrophic outcomes. These safety cases enable collaboration between developers, external experts, and government institutes to establish robust resilience plans without halting innovation. Such frameworks frontload responsibility to ensure minimal disruption while allowing advanced R&D activities to proceed. Nevertheless, the creation of comprehensive safety cases requires significant resource expenditure that could impact smaller labs.
key_points.verbatim: AI safety cases are structured, evidence-based rationales that an AI system deployed to a specific setting is unlikely to cause catastrophic outcomes (Clymer et al. 2024; Buhl et al. 2024; Goemans et al. 2024; Korbak et al. 2025; Balesni et al. 2024).
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve safety assurance during rapid capability scaling by means of structured pre-deployment safety cases.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that proposes structured evidence-based safety cases to demonstrate non-catastrophic operational readiness without hindering rapid capability development. Encompasses: Pre-deployment evaluations, safety case documentation, collaborative resilience planning.

key_points.point: The text outlines structural frameworks for managing internal AI research and development pipelines by separating evaluation teams from executive oversight boards. This procedural architecture draws parallels to traditional engineering research frameworks, such as Federal Aviation Administration experimental aircraft certifications and Nuclear Regulatory Commission research reactor licensing. By establishing structured testing and greenlighting procedures, organizations can maintain rigorous safety protocols without imposing external commercial moratoria. However, heavy administrative layering may introduce development friction if not carefully calibrated to technical iteration speeds.
key_points.verbatim: To perform a flight test, in which a new kind of aircraft is flown in the air as part of the research and development process, manufacturers must apply for a special airworthiness certificate for experimental use (14 CFR º 21.175 1964). Such experimental certificates are issued for flight test R&D activities such as testing new aircraft design concepts, new aircraft equipment, new aircraft installations, new aircraft operating techniques, or new uses for aircraft (14 CFR º 21.191 1964).
key_points.canonical_proposition: Establish internal R&D governance frameworks modeled on aviation and nuclear testing to ensure safe experimentation without blocking deployment.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that models internal AI research and development oversight on established experimental engineering frameworks from aviation and nuclear regulation. Encompasses: experimental certification protocols, safety analysis reporting, structured R&D authorization.

It lists academic papers, research reports, legal documents, and blog posts published between 2013 and 2025. Because the text is purely a reference bibliography, it contains no explicit accelerationist beliefs or doctrinal positions.

By citing works on recursive capability gains and automated scientific discovery, the document implicitly supports the pursuit of technological takeoff.
